units.text: INT. HEDDA - CONTINUOUS
Nor I, thank you.
No, he doesn't either.
[Looks fixedly at him.] But if I say you shall?
It would be of no use.
[Laughing.] Then I, poor creature, have no sort of power over you?
Not in that respect.
But seriously, I think you ought to--for your own sake.
Why, Hedda--!
How so?
Or rather on account of other people.
Indeed?
Otherwise people might be apt to suspect that--in your heart of hearts--you did not feel quite secure--quite confident in yourself.
[Softly.] Oh please, Hedda--!
People may suspect what they like--for the present.
[Joyfully.] Yes, let them!
I saw it plainly in Judge Brack's face a moment ago.
What did you see?
His contemptuous smile, when you dared not go with them into the inner room.
Dared not?
Of course I preferred to stop here and talk to you.
What could be more natural, Hedda?
But the Judge could not guess that.
And I say, too, the way he smiled and glanced at Tesman when you dared not accept his invitation to this wretched little supper-party of his.
Dared not!
Do you say I dared not?
I don't say so.
But that was how Judge Brack understood it.
Well, let him.
Then you are not going with them?
I will stay here with you and Thea.
Yes, Hedda--how can you doubt that?
[Smiles and nods approvingly to LOVBORG.] Firm as a rock!
Faithful to your principles, now and for ever!
Ah, that is how a man should be! [Turns to MRS. ELVSTED and caresses her.] Well now, what did I tell you, when you came to us this morning in such a state of distraction--
[Surprised.] Distraction!
[Terrified.] Hedda--oh Hedda--!
You can see for yourself!
You haven't the slightest reason to be in such mortal terror-- [Interrupting herself.] There!
Now we can all three enjoy ourselves!
[Who has given a start.] Ah--what is all this, Mrs. Tesman?
Oh my God, Hedda!
What are you saying?
What are you doing?
Don't get excited!
That horrid Judge Brack is sitting watching you.
So she was in mortal terror!
On my account!
[Softly and piteously.] Oh, Hedda--now you have ruined everything!
[Looks fixedly at her for a moment.
His face is distorted.] So that was my comrade's frank confidence in me?
[Imploringly.] Oh, my dearest friend--only let me tell you--
[Takes one of the glasses of punch, raises it to his lips, and says in a low, husky voice.] Your health, Thea!
[He empties the glass, puts it down, and takes the second.
[Softly.] Oh, Hedda, Hedda--how could you do this?
I do it?
I ?
Are you crazy?
Here's to your health too, Mrs. Tesman.
Thanks for the truth.
Hurrah for the truth!
[He empties the glass and is about to re-fill it.
[Lays her hand on his arm.] Come, come--no more for the present.
Remember you are going out to supper.
